column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls it “the word of the LORD” and leaves the recipient unnamed; BSB has “a revelation” and supplies Elijah.
The Hebrew locates the brook “before the Jordan”; BSB specifies “east of the Jordan”.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the traveler unnamed and repeats the act of going; BSB supplies Elijah and combines the departure.
The Hebrew repeats bread and meat for morning and evening; BSB names the food once.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the recipient unnamed; BSB supplies Elijah.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the rising and calling man unnamed; BSB names Elijah twice. The vessel is not specified as a cup.
The Hebrew explicitly says to take the bread “in your hand”; BSB leaves the hand implicit.

Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says she, he, and her house ate for days; BSB names Elijah and the woman and describes food being available every day.
The Hebrew describes mediation as “by the hand” of Elijah; BSB leaves the hand image implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew asks “What to me and to you?”; BSB interprets this as “what have you done to me?”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and says he took the child from her bosom; BSB supplies Elijah and has “her arms”.
The Hebrew describes Elijah as living as a stranger with her; BSB says she opened her home to him.
The Hebrew says the child’s soul should return to his inward part; BSB uses “life” and leaves the inward part implicit.
The Hebrew again names the soul and inward part; BSB has “life” returning “to him”.
